title: Choose PrepAhead's new look
question: The roll dealt Takeaway Kraft as the wildcard. Your two briefs, green and yellow, and cute like your reference, sit beside it. Pick one, ask for a mix, or re-roll.

options.label: Takeaway Kraft
options.lineage: kopitiam takeaway packing: kraft bags, rubber stamps, round sticker seals
options.thesis: Every pre-order is a packed kraft bag on the shelf, stamped as it moves.
options.viewport: Kraft header; stalls as white bag labels with a drawn dish and a yellow price seal; tablet leads with 9 trays on a label and orders as bag tags.
options.risk: Brown can read drab or rustic-cafe if the stamp green and seal yellow are timid.

raised.raise: Nothing labelled twice: each figure carries its unit once.
Stalls pack as equal whole cells, never ragged rows.
One colour is reserved for 'yours': your own bag and slot, nothing else.
One message per band: each screen leads with the single next step.
Checking a code dims every other bag tag, so the counter sees one order.

options.label: Pandan & Kaya
options.lineage: the kopitiam kaya toast set: pandan green, kaya yellow, toast crust
options.thesis: Green and yellow from Singapore's own breakfast, with leaf-shaped corners and a tray row that fills as you cook.
options.viewport: Pandan header with 'Skip the lunch queue'; stalls as leaf cards with drawn dishes and kaya price pills; tablet's 9 trays drawn as a row of trays filling green as each is cooked.
options.risk: Green plus yellow can tip into a government eco poster if the leaf motif is overused; it topped my own list.

options.label: Sticker Sheet
options.lineage: die-cut sticker sheets and kawaii stationery, as in your reference
options.thesis: A cheerful sticker sheet: bold outlines, round dish drawings, prices on slapped-on stickers.
options.viewport: Big 'What's for lunch?' headline, coloured pill chips, a two-column dish grid with tilted price stickers and a black pill button; tablet keeps the outlines but calms down.
options.risk: Closest to food-delivery concepts on Behance; outlines everywhere can feel busy on the tablet.

options.label: Boarding Pass
options.lineage: a boarding pass plus the departures board
options.thesis: Your lunch is a boarding pass; the stall's orders are a departures board ranked by slot.
materials: one alert colour that holds until seen
options.viewport: Phone shows the pass (stall as gate, slot as boarding time, code as the scannable block); tablet orders rerank like a board and a changed row stays yellow until seen.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: slots are departures, the code is the boarding block. Strong on clarity, weak on cute.
options.risk: Reads as travel, not lunch, and it is the least cute card here.

options.label: Terminal Yellow
options.thesis: Each screen is the next junction: one yellow band, one decision.
options.viewport: A yellow band reading 'Collect 12:30 · Stall 01', everything else quiet.
options.case: Clear, but airport yellow reads as transit, not lunch, and would drown your green.
options.risk: Feels like a terminal, not a canteen.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Orders as catalogue numbers on matte black, names as colour codes.
options.viewport: A black field with one fac-numbered order and a colour strip.
options.case: Coded colour hides words a busy vendor needs; students don't see themselves in it.
options.risk: Cold and cryptic, the opposite of cute.

options.label: Fair Catalog
options.thesis: Stalls as stamp-size drawings in a numbered grid tied to a canteen map.
options.viewport: A dense grid of tiny stall drawings with a folded canteen map.
options.case: Stamp-size cells are too small for a counter tablet; the fair world is niche.
options.risk: Too dense for a quick lunch order.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: Demand as fixed terrain with today's orders riding over it in purple.
options.viewport: A canteen-as-terrain map with the order course in purple.
options.case: A canteen isn't terrain; map reading adds work for students and vendors.
options.kept: One reserved colour for the active item.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Orders as barcode columns strobing in pure black and white.
options.viewport: A barcode field with one order pulled into focus.
options.case: Pure black-and-white data strobe is the opposite of friendly.
options.risk: Unreadable at a glance and not cute.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A standard food-delivery app: white cards, dish photos, one brand colour.
canonCard.viewport: Search bar, category row, stall cards with photo, rating and time.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every delivery app, and we have no real dish photos.
